57460.e: Gruyère is named after the small town of Gruyères in the Gruyère region. It is a hard cheese and carries the AOP label.
57460.m: Gruyère comes from the Gruyère region.

57461.q: What causes the holes in Emmental cheese?
57461.e: Certain bacteria produce carbon dioxide gas while the cheese ripens. The gas collects in the cheese and leaves round holes.
57461.m: The holes in Emmental are caused by gas from bacteria.

57462.q: What is Appenzeller cheese rubbed with while it ripens?
57462.e: Appenzeller is regularly treated with a herbal brine. The exact recipe is a closely guarded secret.
57462.m: Appenzeller ripens with a secret herbal brine.

57463.q: Which tool is used to scrape fine rosettes off Tête de Moine?
57463.e: Tête de Moine comes from Bellelay in the Bernese Jura. The girolle, a rotating scraper, makes thin rosettes.
57463.m: Tête de Moine is scraped with a girolle.

57464.q: Which soft cheese from the Vallée de Joux is placed in a ring of spruce bark?
57464.e: Vacherin Mont-d'Or is a soft winter cheese from the Vaud Jura. The spruce bark holds it together and gives it a resin-like taste.
57464.m: Vacherin Mont-d'Or sits in a ring of spruce bark.

57465.q: Which very hard cheese from Central Switzerland used to be carried by mule over the Alps to Italy?
57465.e: Sbrinz is an extra-hard cheese from Central Switzerland. Mule drivers carried it over passes such as the Grimsel to Italy.
57465.m: Sbrinz is an extra-hard cheese from Central Switzerland.

57466.q: Which cheese from eastern Switzerland is named after a town in former East Prussia?
57466.e: At the end of the 19th century, cheesemakers brought the recipe from Tilsit to Thurgau. Since then Swiss Tilsiter has been made in eastern Switzerland.
57466.m: Tilsiter is named after the town of Tilsit.

57467.q: What does the AOP label on a cheese guarantee?
a: It comes from a particular region
57467.e: AOP stands for “Appellation d'Origine Protégée”, meaning protected designation of origin. Production and raw materials must come from the set region.
57467.m: AOP protects where a product comes from.

57468.q: Which two cheeses make up “moitié-moitié” fondue?
57468.e: “Moitié-moitié” means “half and half”. This Fribourg fondue is made half with Gruyère and half with Vacherin fribourgeois.
57468.m: Moitié-moitié is half Gruyère and half Vacherin.

57469.q: Which lake is the Lavaux wine region on?
57469.e: Lavaux stretches between Lausanne and Vevey along the northern shore of Lake Geneva. The vineyards drop down to the lake in steep terraces.

57470.q: Which list do the Lavaux vineyard terraces belong to?
a: New Seven Wonders of the World
57470.e: UNESCO added Lavaux to the World Heritage list in 2007. It honours a landscape that people have shaped over centuries.
57470.m: Lavaux is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

57471.q: Who built the first terraces in Lavaux in the Middle Ages?
57471.e: In the 12th century, Cistercian monks began turning the steep slopes into terraces with walls. That is how the vineyards you can see today came about.
57471.m: Monks built the first terraces in Lavaux.

57472.q: Which “three suns” help the grapes in Lavaux ripen well?
a: Sun, reflection from the lake and warm walls
Sun, föhn wind and bise wind
57472.e: The vines get direct sunlight, light reflected back from the lake and the warmth of the stone walls. These three sources of warmth are called the three suns.
57472.m: In Lavaux, sun, lake and walls warm the vines.

57474.q: What is the Valais white wine made from the Chasselas grape called?
57474.e: In Valais, Chasselas is traditionally called “Fendant”. It is one of the best-known wines of the canton.
57474.m: Fendant is the Valais name for Chasselas.

57475.q: Why can vines grow in Valais even above 1000 metres?
a: Because it is very sunny and dry there
Because it rains a lot there
Because a warm sea wind blows
57475.e: The high mountains keep the rain out, and the sun shines often. That is why in Visperterminen vines grow up to about 1100 metres.
57475.m: Sun and dryness let vines grow high up in Valais.

57476.q: What are the old water channels called that are used to water meadows and vines in dry Valais?
57476.e: Valais is very dry because the high mountains keep the rain out. The Suonen, called “bisses” in French, carry glacier water to fields and vineyards.
57476.m: Suonen bring water to meadows and vines in Valais.

57477.q: Which religious refugees brought the craft of watchmaking to Geneva in the 16th century?
57477.e: The Huguenots were Protestant Christians from France who were persecuted. Many fled to Geneva and brought their skills as watchmakers with them.

57478.q: Why did many farming families in the Jura use to make watch parts?
a: There was little field work in the long winter
Only farmers were allowed to build watches
The ground was full of gold
There were no cows in the Jura
57478.e: Winters in the Jura are long and snowy. During this time the farmers earned extra money by making watch parts at home.
57478.m: Long winters made the Jura a watchmaking region.

57479.q: Which two Jura towns have been UNESCO World Heritage “watchmaking towns” since 2009?
57479.e: La Chaux-de-Fonds and Le Locle were rebuilt in a grid pattern after a fire. The houses and streets are designed entirely around the work of watchmakers.
57479.m: La Chaux-de-Fonds and Le Locle are World Heritage watchmaking towns.

57480.q: What caused the great crisis of the Swiss watch industry in the 1970s?
a: Cheap quartz watches from Asia and the USA
A big earthquake in the Jura
57480.e: Quartz watches were more accurate and cheaper than mechanical watches. Tens of thousands of jobs in the Swiss watch industry were lost.
57480.m: Quartz watches caused the watch crisis of the 1970s.

57481.q: Which cheap plastic watch helped to save the Swiss watch industry from 1983?
57481.e: The Swatch was a colourful, low-priced quartz watch made of just a few parts. It became a fashion item and gave the industry new energy.
57481.m: The Swatch helped the Swiss watch industry from 1983.

57482.q: In which bilingual town at the southern foot of the Jura does the Swatch Group have its headquarters?
57482.e: Biel/Bienne is an important centre of the watch industry. Several large watchmakers have their headquarters here.
57482.m: Biel is an important watchmaking town.

57483.q: In which high valley in the Vaud Jura are especially complicated watches made?
57483.e: In the Vallée de Joux, with places like Le Sentier and Le Brassus, famous watch manufacturers have their base. They build watches with many extra functions.
57483.m: Complicated watches are made in the Vallée de Joux.

57484.q: What does the label “Swiss made” on a watch mean?
a: The watch was mostly made in Switzerland
The watch is made of Swiss gold
The watch only shows Swiss time
The watch was sold in Switzerland
57484.e: A watch may only be called “Swiss made” if the movement is Swiss and at least 60 percent of the manufacturing costs arise in Switzerland.
57484.m: “Swiss made” means mostly made in Switzerland.

57485.q: Which two big pharmaceutical companies have their headquarters in Basel?
57485.e: Roche and Novartis are among the largest pharmaceutical companies in the world. Both have their headquarters in Basel.
57485.m: Roche and Novartis are the Basel pharma giants.

57486.q: From which branch of industry did Basel's chemical and pharmaceutical industry develop in the 19th century?
57486.e: In Basel, artificial dyes were first made for silk ribbon weaving. This knowledge later led to companies making chemicals and medicines.
57486.m: Basel's pharma industry grew out of the dye industry.

57487.q: What do Basel pharmaceutical companies like Novartis and Roche mainly make?
57487.e: Pharmaceutical companies research active ingredients and make medicines. Novartis and Roche are among the largest in the world.

57488.q: How tall is the Roche tower “Building 2” in Basel, the tallest building in Switzerland (as of 2025)?
57488.e: Roche's Building 2 was finished in 2022 and is 205 metres tall. That makes it taller than the neighbouring Building 1 at 178 metres.
57488.m: At 205 metres, Roche's Building 2 is the tallest building in Switzerland.

57489.q: Which group of goods makes up the largest part of Swiss exports?
57489.e: Medicines and other chemical and pharmaceutical products make up around half of Swiss goods exports. A large share comes from the Basel region.
57489.m: Pharmaceutical products are Switzerland's most important export.

57490.q: Which neighbouring countries do many of the cross-border commuters who work in Basel come from?
57490.e: Basel lies where three countries meet. Every day, many people commute from Alsace and southern Baden to work at Basel companies.
57490.m: Many cross-border commuters in Basel come from Germany and France.

57491.q: What happened in 1986 when a chemical warehouse burned down in Schweizerhalle near Basel?
a: Poisonous firefighting water polluted the Rhine
An earthquake destroyed the old town
57491.e: During the fire in a Sandoz warehouse, a lot of poison got into the Rhine with the firefighting water. Fish died along many kilometres of the river.
57491.m: The Schweizerhalle fire in 1986 poisoned the Rhine.

57492.q: Which authority in Switzerland checks whether a new medicine is approved?
57492.e: Swissmedic is the Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products in Bern. It checks whether medicines are safe and effective before they may be sold.

57493.q: Which square in Zurich is seen as the symbol of Swiss banking?
57493.e: The headquarters of big banks stand on Paradeplatz. It is on Bahnhofstrasse in the middle of Zurich.
57493.m: Paradeplatz is the symbol of Zurich as a financial centre.

57494.q: What is the name of the Swiss stock exchange based in Zurich?
57494.e: Shares and other securities are traded on the SIX Swiss Exchange. It is the most important stock exchange in Switzerland.
57494.m: The Swiss stock exchange is called the SIX Swiss Exchange.

57495.q: What does the abbreviation SMI stand for?
57495.e: The SMI shows how the share prices of the 20 largest companies on the Swiss stock exchange are doing. It is the most important share index in Switzerland.
57495.m: The SMI is the most important share index in Switzerland.

57496.q: Which bank took over Credit Suisse in 2023?
57496.e: Credit Suisse ran into a serious crisis in 2023. With support from the federal government it was taken over by UBS.
57496.m: UBS took over Credit Suisse in 2023.

57497.q: What does a reinsurance company, such as one based in Zurich, do?
a: It pays pensions to retired people
57497.e: A reinsurance company takes on part of the risks of other insurers. That way they are covered even in big disasters.

57498.q: In which two cities does the Swiss National Bank have its seat?
57498.e: By law, the Swiss National Bank has its seat in Bern and Zurich. It makes sure the franc stays stable.
57498.m: The National Bank is based in Bern and Zurich.

57499.q: Which economic sector do banks and insurance companies belong to?
57499.e: Banks and insurers do not make goods; they offer services. That is why they belong to the tertiary sector, the service sector.
57499.m: Banks belong to the service sector.

57500.q: What did Swiss banking secrecy mean?
a: Banks had to keep information about customers secret
Banks were not allowed to pay interest
Only Swiss people could have an account
57500.e: Banking secrecy obliges banks not to pass on customer data. Towards foreign tax authorities it was greatly relaxed from 2017 with the automatic exchange of information.
57500.m: Banking secrecy protects banks' customer data.

57501.q: Which natural resource is extracted in Switzerland, for example in Bex and near Basel?
57501.e: The Swiss salt works extract salt in Schweizerhalle, Riburg and Bex. It is used as table salt, in industry and for gritting roads.
57501.m: Salt is one of Switzerland's few natural resources.

57502.q: Where do the oil and gas used in Switzerland come from?
a: From drilling in the Central Plateau
57502.e: Switzerland does not produce any oil or gas itself. Everything has to be brought in by pipeline, ship, rail or lorry.
57502.m: Switzerland has to import oil and gas.

57503.q: Which home-grown energy source supplies more than half of Switzerland's electricity?
57503.e: Reservoirs and river power stations use the power of water from the mountains. They produce most of Switzerland's electricity.
57503.m: Hydropower is Switzerland's most important source of electricity.

57504.q: Which raw material is extracted in the largest amounts in Switzerland?
57504.e: The glaciers of the ice ages left lots of gravel and sand in the Central Plateau. It is mainly used to make concrete for building.
57504.m: Gravel and sand are important Swiss raw materials.

57505.q: How does Switzerland make up economically for its lack of raw materials?
a: It turns raw materials into valuable products
57505.e: Switzerland imports raw materials and makes high-quality products from them, such as medicines, machines and watches. Well-trained specialists are important for this.
57505.m: Switzerland turns imported raw materials into valuable products.

57506.q: Which canton, besides Geneva, is a centre of world commodity trading?
57506.e: Many large companies that trade in oil, metals and grain are based in Zug and Geneva. The goods themselves usually never come to Switzerland.
57506.m: Zug and Geneva are centres of commodity trading.

57507.q: Which mountain near Sargans was an iron ore mine until 1966?
57507.e: Iron ore was mined for centuries at the Gonzen in the St Gallen Rhine Valley. The mine closed in 1966 and can be visited today.
57507.m: Iron ore was mined at the Gonzen until 1966.

57508.q: Which renewable raw material comes from the forests that cover about a third of Switzerland?
57508.e: Around a third of the country is covered by forest. The wood is used as building material, for furniture and for heating.
57508.m: Wood is an important home-grown raw material.

57509.q: Along which river do goods travel by ship from the sea to the ports in Basel?
57509.e: The Swiss Rhine ports in Basel are linked via the Rhine to Rotterdam on the North Sea. That is how heating oil, grain and containers come into the country.
57509.m: The Rhine connects Switzerland with the sea.

57510.q: In which Graubünden town is the Spengler Cup ice hockey tournament held every year at the end of December?
57510.e: The Spengler Cup is one of the oldest ice hockey tournaments in the world. It has been held in Davos since 1923.
57510.m: The Spengler Cup takes place in Davos.

57511.q: In which village in the Bernese Oberland is the Lauberhorn race held?
57511.e: The Lauberhorn race in Wengen has the longest downhill in the Alpine Ski World Cup. Every January it attracts lots of spectators.
57511.m: The Lauberhorn race takes place in Wengen.

57512.q: On which slope in Adelboden is a World Cup giant slalom held every year?
57512.e: Every January the best skiers race the giant slalom on the Chuenisbärgli in Adelboden. The steep finish slope is famous.
57512.m: World Cup pros race the giant slalom on the Chuenisbärgli in Adelboden.

57513.q: Which Valais resort hosts the 2027 Alpine World Ski Championships?
57513.e: The 2027 Alpine World Ski Championships take place in Crans-Montana. The resort already hosted the championships in 1987.
57513.m: Crans-Montana hosts the 2027 World Ski Championships.

57514.q: What do many ski resorts use when there is too little snow because of climate change?
57514.e: Snow cannons spray water that freezes into artificial snow in the cold air. They need a lot of water and electricity.

57515.q: On which mountain near Engelberg did the world's first rotating cable car run in 1992?
57515.e: The “Rotair” cabin on the Titlis turns all the way round once during the ride. That way all passengers see the whole panorama.
57515.m: The world's first rotating cable car ran on the Titlis.

57516.q: Which ski area in Graubünden is especially known for its freestyle snow parks?
57516.e: Laax has big snow parks and a huge halfpipe. International snowboard and freeski competitions are held there too.
57516.m: Laax is known for its snow parks.

57517.q: Which car-free holiday resort in Valais is also called the “Pearl of the Alps”?
57517.e: Saas-Fee lies at around 1800 metres and is surrounded by many four-thousand-metre peaks. No petrol cars drive in the village.
57517.m: Saas-Fee is the Pearl of the Alps.

57518.q: How did people get to Zermatt before the railway was built in 1891?
a: On foot, by mule or by carriage
57518.e: Before the railway from Visp to Zermatt was built, there was only a narrow path through the valley. Travellers walked or took mules and carriages.
57518.m: A railway has run to Zermatt since 1891.

57519.q: How do most visitors get to Zermatt, since the village is car-free?
57519.e: Cars have to stay in Täsch. From there a shuttle train runs to Zermatt, and only small electric vehicles drive in the village.
57519.m: You reach Zermatt without a car, for example by train.

57520.q: Who first climbed to the summit of the Matterhorn in 1865?
a: A team led by Edward Whymper
A team led by Edmund Hillary
A team led by Reinhold Messner
A team led by Horace-Bénédict de Saussure
57520.e: The Englishman Edward Whymper reached the summit in 1865 with six companions. On the way down, four of them fell to their deaths.
57520.m: Edward Whymper was the first to stand on the Matterhorn in 1865.

57521.q: Which kind of railway runs from Zermatt up to the Gornergrat?
57521.e: The Gornergrat railway has been running since 1898. Using a cog wheel, it climbs the steep route to over 3000 metres.
57521.m: A rack railway runs up to the Gornergrat.

57522.q: What is the top station on the Klein Matterhorn at 3883 metres?
a: The highest cable car station in Europe
The highest railway station in the world
57522.e: The Matterhorn Glacier Paradise station is at 3883 metres. It is the highest cable car station in Europe.
57522.m: Europe's highest cable car station is on the Klein Matterhorn.

57523.q: Which famous panoramic train links Zermatt with St Moritz?
57523.e: The Glacier Express takes about eight hours for the journey. That is why it is often called the “slowest express train in the world”.
57523.m: The Glacier Express runs from Zermatt to St Moritz.

57524.e: Zermatt lies at the very end of the Matter Valley, which joins the Rhone Valley at Visp. It belongs to the canton of Valais.
57524.m: Zermatt lies at the far end of the Matter Valley.

57525.q: Which river flows from Zermatt down through the Matter Valley towards Visp?
57525.e: The Matter Vispa forms from the meltwater of the glaciers around Zermatt. At Stalden it joins the Saaser Vispa to form the Vispa.
57525.m: The Matter Vispa flows through Zermatt.

57526.q: Who started winter tourism in St Moritz with a bet in 1864?
57526.e: Badrutt invited English summer guests to come back in winter. If they did not like it, he would pay for their journey, but they stayed, delighted, until Easter.
57526.m: Winter tourism in St Moritz began with Badrutt's bet in 1864.

57527.q: In which year did St Moritz last host the Alpine World Ski Championships (as of 2025)?
57527.e: St Moritz has hosted the Alpine World Ski Championships several times, most recently in 2017. The races took place on its local mountain, Corviglia.
57527.m: St Moritz hosted the World Ski Championships in 2017.

57528.q: Which railway line from St Moritz to Tirano is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
57528.e: The Albula and Bernina lines of the Rhaetian Railway have been UNESCO World Heritage since 2008. The Bernina line crosses the Bernina Pass without a cog wheel.
57528.m: The Bernina line links St Moritz with Tirano.

57529.q: What is special about the bobsleigh run from St Moritz to Celerina?
a: It is built from natural ice every year
It is made entirely of wood
It can be used in summer
57529.e: The Olympic bob run is rebuilt by hand from snow and water every winter. It is the only natural ice track for bobsleigh in the World Cup.
57529.m: The St Moritz bob run is made of natural ice.

57530.q: What happens at the “White Turf” in St Moritz?
a: Horse races on the frozen lake
57530.e: At White Turf, racehorses gallop across the frozen Lake St Moritz. The races have taken place in February for over 100 years.
57530.m: At White Turf, horses race across the frozen lake.

57531.q: What did the Hotel Kulm in St Moritz have in 1878 for the first time in Switzerland?
57531.e: Johannes Badrutt had a small hydropower station built for the Hotel Kulm. That is where the first electric light in Switzerland shone.
57531.m: Switzerland's first electric light shone in St Moritz.

57532.q: Which sport is done at the Engadin Skimarathon?
57532.e: Every March, thousands of cross-country skiers race from Maloja to S-chanf in the Engadin Skimarathon. The course is 42 kilometres long.
57532.m: The Engadin Skimarathon is a cross-country skiing race.

57533.q: What was St Moritz already known for before winter tourism?
57533.e: The iron-rich mineral spring of St Moritz was used centuries ago. Summer guests came to the Engadine to take the cure.
57533.m: St Moritz was first a spa town with a healing spring.

57534.q: What is the famous ice run in St Moritz called, which you ride down lying on your front, head first?
57534.e: The Cresta Run was built by English guests in 1884. You ride a heavy sled lying on your stomach, head first.
57534.m: You ride the Cresta Run lying on your front.

57535.q: What can visitors see on the Schynige Platte above Interlaken?
57535.e: Hundreds of plant species from the Alps grow in the Schynige Platte alpine garden. An old rack railway goes up from Wilderswil.
57535.m: There is an alpine garden on the Schynige Platte.

57536.q: What is the railway station on the Jungfraujoch at 3454 metres called?
57536.e: The Jungfraujoch is the highest railway station in Europe. Since 1912 the Jungfrau Railway has travelled up through a tunnel in the Eiger and Mönch.
57536.m: The Jungfraujoch is called Top of Europe.

57538.q: Which three famous mountains can you see from the area around Interlaken?
57538.e: Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau form the well-known mountain chain of the Bernese Oberland. Their panorama attracts visitors from all over the world.
57538.m: Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau shape the Bernese Oberland.

57539.q: What does the name Interlaken mean?
57539.e: The name comes from the Latin “inter lacus”, which means “between the lakes”. The town lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz.

57540.q: Which large glacier is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch?
57540.e: The Great Aletsch Glacier is the largest glacier in the Alps. The area has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2001.
57540.m: The Aletsch Glacier is the largest glacier in the Alps.

57541.q: At which festival in Interlaken is a heavy stone thrown as far as possible?
57541.e: At the Unspunnen Festival, the Unspunnen stone, which weighs around 83 kilograms, is thrown. The festival only takes place every few years.
57541.m: The Unspunnen stone is thrown at the Unspunnen Festival.

57542.q: Which waterfalls near Lauterbrunnen thunder down inside a mountain?
57542.e: The Trümmelbach Falls carry the meltwater from the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau. They roar through gorges in the rock and can be reached by lifts and paths.
57542.m: The Trümmelbach Falls flow inside the mountain.

57543.q: What is special about the Swiss National Park in the whole Alpine region?
a: It is the oldest national park in the Alps.
It is the largest national park in the Alps.
It is the highest park in Europe.
It is the only park with glaciers.
57543.e: The national park in the Engadine opened in 1914. It is the oldest national park in the Alps and in Central Europe.
57543.m: The Swiss National Park is the oldest national park in the Alps.

57544.q: Roughly how high is the highest peak in the Swiss National Park?
57544.e: The highest peak in the park is Piz Pisoc at 3174 m. The lowest point is at about 1400 m.
57544.m: The highest peak in the national park is about 3200 metres high.

57545.q: Which mountain pass road runs right through the Swiss National Park?
57545.e: The road over the Ofen Pass links Zernez with the Val Müstair and runs straight through the park.
57545.m: The Ofen Pass road runs through the national park.

57546.q: Roughly how big is the Swiss National Park?
57546.e: The park covers about 170 km² today. When it was founded it was less than half that size.
57546.m: The national park is about 170 square kilometres in size.

57547.q: Which region is the Swiss National Park in?
57547.e: The national park lies in the Engadine in the canton of Graubünden, near Zernez. Its oldest part is the Val Cluozza.
57547.m: The Swiss National Park is in the Engadine.

57548.q: Which rule applies to hikers in the Swiss National Park?
a: You must not leave the paths.
You may light a fire anywhere.
You may sleep in a tent.
57548.e: Strict rules apply in the park: you must stay on the marked paths. Picking plants, lighting fires and staying overnight are forbidden.
57548.m: In the national park you always stay on the marked paths.

57549.q: Why are no meadows mown and no trees cut down in the Swiss National Park?
a: Nature should develop without human interference.
There are no meadows or trees in the park.
The work is too expensive there.
The farmers have no time for it.
57549.e: In the national park, nature is left to itself. People are only observers on the marked paths, so that natural processes can be studied.
57549.m: In the national park nature may develop freely.

57550.q: Which organisation, then called the “Swiss League for Nature Protection”, was founded in 1909 to pay for the national park?
57550.e: The Swiss League for Nature Protection raised money for the planned park. Today the organisation is called Pro Natura.
57550.m: Pro Natura was founded in 1909 to support the national park.

57551.q: What is allowed in the Swiss National Park?
57551.e: In the national park you may only hike on the marked paths. Dogs, collecting and riding off the paths are forbidden so that the animals are left in peace.
57551.m: In the national park you only hike on marked paths.

57552.q: Which high railway station is on the edge of the Jungfrau-Aletsch World Heritage Site?
57552.e: The Jungfraujoch is at around 3450 metres above sea level and is the highest railway station in Europe. From there you can look down on the Aletsch Glacier.
57552.m: From the Jungfraujoch you can see the Aletsch Glacier.

57553.q: Roughly how big has the Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch World Heritage Site been since it was enlarged in 2007?
57553.e: In 2007 the area was enlarged from around 540 km² to around 824 km². That makes it much bigger than the Swiss National Park.
57553.m: The Jungfrau-Aletsch World Heritage Site is about 820 square kilometres.

57554.q: Which two cantons does the UNESCO World Heritage Site Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch cover?
57554.e: The area lies in the Bernese Oberland and in Upper Valais. The Aletsch Glacier flows on the Valais side.
57554.m: The Jungfrau-Aletsch World Heritage Site is in the cantons of Bern and Valais.

57555.q: What was special about the Jungfrau-Aletsch World Heritage Site when it was added in 2001?
a: First natural heritage site in the Alps
First cultural heritage site in Switzerland
First World Heritage Site in Europe
First World Heritage Site in a city
57555.e: Jungfrau-Aletsch was the first UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site in the whole Alpine region.
57555.m: Jungfrau-Aletsch was the first natural World Heritage Site in the Alps.

57556.q: What does it mean that Jungfrau-Aletsch is a UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site?
a: Its nature is seen as unique for all of humanity.
The area now belongs to the UN.
Nobody may enter the area any more.
Nobody may live in the area any more.
57556.e: UNESCO adds areas whose nature is unique in the world. Switzerland promises to protect and preserve this landscape.
57556.m: A natural World Heritage Site is a natural landscape that is unique in the world.

57557.q: What is the name of the highest mountain in the Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch World Heritage Site?
57557.e: At 4274 m, the Finsteraarhorn is the highest peak in the area and in the Bernese Alps.
57557.m: The Finsteraarhorn is the highest mountain in the Bernese Alps.

57558.q: Which trees are typical of the old Aletsch Forest?
57558.e: Mainly Swiss stone pines and larches grow in the Aletsch Forest. Some of the stone pines are almost 1000 years old.
57558.m: Old Swiss stone pines and larches grow in the Aletsch Forest.

a: An old, protected mountain forest by the Aletsch Glacier
A ski area in the Jura
57559.e: The Aletsch Forest lies above the Aletsch Glacier and has been a nature reserve since 1933.
57559.m: The Aletsch Forest is a protected mountain forest.

57560.q: Why has the Great Aletsch Glacier been getting shorter for decades?
57560.e: As it gets warmer, more ice melts in summer than new ice forms in winter. That is why the glacier is retreating.
57560.m: Global warming is making the Aletsch Glacier shrink.

57561.q: What is the Swiss Tectonic Arena Sardona?
a: A UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Alps
A ski area on the Säntis
57561.e: The Tectonic Arena Sardona has been a UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site since 2008. You can see especially well there how the Alps were formed.
57561.m: The Tectonic Arena Sardona is a World Heritage Site in the Alps.

57562.q: Which three cantons is the Tectonic Arena Sardona in?
57562.e: The World Heritage Site stretches across municipalities in the cantons of Glarus, St Gallen and Graubünden.
57562.m: The Tectonic Arena Sardona links Glarus, St Gallen and Graubünden.

57563.q: What is the Tectonic Arena Sardona famous all over the world for?
a: Older rock lies on top of younger rock.
The deepest lake in Europe is there.
You can find dinosaur eggs there.
57563.e: At the Glarus thrust, old rock was pushed over much younger rock. This shows how mountains are formed by pushing.
57563.m: In the Tectonic Arena Sardona, old rock lies on top of young rock.

57564.q: What is the clearly visible rock boundary that makes the Tectonic Arena Sardona famous called?
57564.e: The Glarus thrust can be seen as a sharp line in the rock faces. It shows where layers of rock were pushed over each other.
57564.m: The Glarus thrust shows how the Alps were pushed up.

57565.q: What colour is the very old rock that lies on top in the Tectonic Arena Sardona?
57565.e: The reddish rock is called Verrucano and is around 250 to 300 million years old. It lies on top of much younger rock.
57565.m: Reddish, very old rock lies on top in the Tectonic Arena.

57567.q: What do geologists study in the Tectonic Arena Sardona?
a: What the weather will be like
57567.e: Geologists study rocks and how they were formed. In the Tectonic Arena Sardona, Albert Heim, for example, studied how the Alps were pushed up.
57567.m: In the Tectonic Arena Sardona, people study how the Alps were formed.

57568.q: Which mountain is the Tectonic Arena Sardona named after?
57568.e: Piz Sardona is one of the three-thousand-metre peaks in the area and gave the World Heritage Site its name.
57568.m: The Tectonic Arena is named after Piz Sardona.

57569.q: In geology, what do you call a large slab of rock that has been pushed over other rocks?
57569.e: A nappe is a huge mass of rock that has been pushed a long way over other layers. The Alps are made up of many such nappes.
57569.m: The Alps are made of nappes pushed on top of each other.

57570.q: Why is Monte San Giorgio a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
57570.e: Thousands of very well preserved fossils of sea creatures from the Triassic were found on Monte San Giorgio.
57570.m: Monte San Giorgio is famous for its fossils.

57571.q: Roughly how old are the fossils from Monte San Giorgio?
57571.e: The fossils come from the Triassic and are around 240 million years old. The first dinosaurs also lived at that time.
57571.m: The fossils from Monte San Giorgio are about 240 million years old.

57572.q: Where did most of the animals live whose fossils are found on Monte San Giorgio?
57572.e: Around 240 million years ago there was a sea lagoon there. That is why mainly fish and marine reptiles are found.
57572.m: There used to be a sea at Monte San Giorgio.

57574.q: Which marine reptile from Monte San Giorgio is an ichthyosaur?
57574.e: Mixosaurus belongs to the ichthyosaurs, the “fish lizards”. Several hundred specimens have been found on Monte San Giorgio.
57574.m: Mixosaurus is an ichthyosaur from Monte San Giorgio.

57575.q: What can you see in the museum at Monte San Giorgio?
57575.e: The fossil museum in Meride shows fossilised fish, ichthyosaurs and other marine reptiles from Monte San Giorgio.
57575.m: At Monte San Giorgio you can see fossilised sea creatures.

57576.q: Which organisation awards the title “biosphere reserve”?
57576.e: Biosphere reserves are part of the UNESCO programme “Man and the Biosphere”. Nature and the economy are meant to be in harmony there.
57576.m: Biosphere reserves are recognised by UNESCO.

57578.q: Which canton is the Biosfera Engiadina Val Müstair in?
57578.e: The Biosfera lies in the Lower Engadine and the Val Müstair in the east of Graubünden. The national park is also part of it.
57578.m: The Biosfera Engiadina Val Müstair is in Graubünden.

57579.q: Which three zones is a biosphere reserve divided into?
a: Core zone, buffer zone, transition zone
Mountain zone, valley zone, lake zone
Wild zone, free zone, town zone
Forest zone, meadow zone, field zone
57579.e: In the core zone, nature comes first. In the buffer zone the land is used gently, and in the transition zone people live and work.
57579.m: A biosphere reserve has a core zone, a buffer zone and a transition zone.

57580.q: Which area forms the core zone of the Biosfera Engiadina Val Müstair?
57580.e: Together with the Val Müstair and areas of Scuol, the national park forms a biosphere reserve. The national park is the strictly protected core zone.
57580.m: The national park is the core zone of the Engiadina Val Müstair biosphere.

57581.q: What is the aim of a biosphere reserve?
a: To protect nature and use it sustainably
To protect only animals, without people
To build as many roads as possible
57581.e: People live and work in a biosphere reserve. They should use nature in a way that preserves it.
57581.m: In a biosphere, people live in harmony with nature.

57582.q: Which Swiss area became Switzerland's first UNESCO biosphere reserve in 1979?
57582.e: In 1979 the national park was the first area in Switzerland to be declared a biosphere reserve.
57582.m: Switzerland got its first biosphere reserve in 1979.

57583.q: What is the UNESCO programme that biosphere reserves belong to called?
57583.e: The “Man and the Biosphere” programme, MAB for short, started around 1970 and links biosphere reserves around the world.
57583.m: Biosphere reserves belong to the “Man and the Biosphere” programme.

57584.q: Which three categories does federal law use for parks of national importance?
a: National park, regional nature park, nature discovery park
City park, country park, mountain park
Theme park, water park, adventure park
57584.e: The Federal Act on the Protection of Nature and Cultural Heritage has three categories. Regional nature parks are the most common.
57584.m: Parks of national importance are national parks, nature parks or nature discovery parks.

57585.q: Which federal office awards the label “park of national importance”?
57585.e: The FOEN checks the regions' applications and awards the park label. It also supports the parks with money.
57585.m: The Federal Office for the Environment awards the park label.

57586.q: Which regional nature park in Graubünden is considered the largest nature park in Switzerland?
57586.e: Parc Ela lies in central Graubünden around the Albula Pass and the Julier Pass. By area it is the largest nature park in Switzerland.
57586.m: Parc Ela is the largest nature park in Switzerland.

57587.q: Which park near Zurich is a nature discovery park?
57587.e: A nature discovery park lies close to a city. Wildnispark Zürich Sihlwald was the first nature discovery park in Switzerland.
57587.m: The Sihlwald is a nature discovery park near Zurich.

57588.q: What is typical of a regional nature park?
a: People live and work in the park.
The park is in the middle of a city.
There are only zoo animals in the park.
57588.e: A regional nature park is a lived-in rural region with beautiful nature and culture. Its economy should be strengthened in a sustainable way.
57588.m: People live and work in a regional nature park.

57589.q: Which canton is the Pfyn-Finges Nature Park, with a large pine forest on the Rhone, in?
57589.e: The Pfyn-Finges Nature Park lies between Leuk and Sierre on the German-French language border in Valais.
57589.m: The Pfyn-Finges Nature Park is in Valais.

57590.q: How many national parks does Switzerland have?
57590.e: Switzerland has only one national park, the Swiss National Park in Graubünden. A second one, the Parc Adula, was rejected in 2016.
57590.m: Switzerland has just one national park.

57592.q: In which Graubünden town is the institute that publishes the avalanche bulletin every day in winter?
57592.e: The WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF in Davos assesses the avalanche danger in the Swiss Alps every day.
57592.m: The avalanche bulletin comes from Davos.

57593.q: Which type of avalanche causes the most deaths among winter sports enthusiasts?
57593.e: In a slab avalanche, a whole slab of snow breaks away at once. Usually the victims trigger it themselves.
57593.m: Slab avalanches are the most dangerous for winter sports enthusiasts.

57594.q: From roughly what slope angle can slab avalanches break away?
57594.e: Slab avalanches usually break away on slopes steeper than about 30 degrees. That is why steepness matters when planning a tour.
57594.m: Slopes from about 30 degrees are at risk of avalanches.

57595.q: Which device do ski tourers carry so that they can be found quickly after an avalanche?
57595.e: The avalanche transceiver sends out a signal. Companions can use it to locate people buried in the snow. A shovel and probe are also part of the kit.
57595.m: An avalanche transceiver helps find buried people quickly.

57596.q: Why is a quick rescue so important when someone is buried by an avalanche?
a: The chance of survival drops sharply after about 15 minutes.
The snow turns into water after an hour.
The avalanche always slides on after ten minutes.
Rescue helicopters may only fly for a short time.
57596.e: Most buried people survive the first few minutes. After about 15 minutes the chance drops sharply because air runs out.
57596.m: In an avalanche, every minute counts.

57597.q: What are the steel grids or wooden walls on steep slopes above many mountain villages?
57597.e: Avalanche barriers hold the snow in place where avalanches start. That way no big avalanche can form at all.
57597.m: Avalanche barriers hold the snow on the slope.

57598.q: Why were there so many avalanches in the Swiss Alps in the avalanche winter of 1951?
a: A huge amount of snow fell in a short time.
It was warm and dry all winter.
Many new ski lifts were built.
57598.e: In January and February 1951 it snowed very heavily for days. The masses of snow set off many large avalanches, and almost 100 people died.
57598.m: Lots of new snow in a short time increases the avalanche danger.

57599.q: What most often triggers a debris flow?
57599.e: In heavy rain or thunderstorms, loose material in steep gullies gets soaked and starts to slide. Melting snow can also trigger debris flows.
57599.m: Heavy rain is the most common trigger of debris flows.

57601.q: What do you call a large basin in front of a village that catches the stones and rubble of a debris flow?
57601.e: A debris retention basin holds back stones and mud while the water flows on. It has to be dug out after an event.
57601.m: Debris retention basins protect villages from debris flows.

57602.q: In which season are there the most debris flows in the Alps?
a: Debris flows only happen in January
57602.e: In summer, thunderstorms often bring heavy rain. On top of that, the ground thaws high up. That is why debris flows happen most often then.
57602.m: Debris flows happen mainly in summer during thunderstorms.

57603.q: Why does global warming tend to cause more debris flows in high mountains?
a: The permafrost thaws and loosens rubble.
57603.e: Permafrost is ground that is frozen all year round and holds rubble together. When it thaws, the material becomes loose and can slide more easily.
57603.m: Thawing permafrost makes debris flows more likely.

57604.q: What is a debris flow often called in the local dialect in Graubünden and eastern Switzerland?
57604.e: In Graubünden and eastern Switzerland people speak of a Rüfe. Many place names and field names are a reminder of this.
57604.m: In Graubünden a debris flow is often called a Rüfe.

57605.q: Why can a debris flow carry bigger boulders than a normal flood?
a: The mixture is much denser and heavier than water.
It always flows more slowly than water.
It is made only of ice.
57605.e: A debris flow contains a lot of solid material, which makes it dense and heavy. That is why it can even carry blocks the size of houses.
57605.m: A debris flow is much heavier than pure water.

57606.q: What caused the big floods on the northern side of the Alps in August 2005?
a: A storm surge from the sea
57606.e: In August 2005 it rained very heavily for several days. Rivers and lakes burst their banks, and the damage came to around 3 billion francs.
57606.m: Heavy, lasting rain led to big floods in 2005.

57607.q: Which district of Bern on the Aare was flooded in 1999 and 2005?
57607.e: The Matte lies low down, right by the Aare. That is why it was under water in both floods.
57607.m: The Matte district in Bern lies right by the Aare.

57608.q: What does a hazard map show?
a: Where natural hazards such as floods threaten
Where the best hiking trails are
Where the borders of the cantons run
57608.e: Hazard maps use colours to show how much danger an area is in. Red means considerable danger, and usually no new building is allowed there.
57608.m: Hazard maps show areas at risk.

57609.q: Which colour means “considerable danger” on a Swiss hazard map?
57609.e: Red stands for considerable danger, blue for medium danger and yellow for low danger.
57609.m: Red on the hazard map means considerable danger.

57610.q: What does the term “hundred-year flood” mean?
a: A flood that happens on average about every 100 years
A flood that lasts exactly 100 days
A flood that can only happen once per century
57610.e: The term describes probability: statistically, a flood this big happens about once in 100 years. But it can also happen twice in a short time.
57610.m: A hundred-year flood happens on average about every 100 years.

57611.q: What does a gauge on a river or lake measure?
57611.e: A gauge shows how high the water is. If the level rises quickly, a flood may be on the way.
57611.m: A gauge shows the water level.

57612.q: Why does modern flood protection often give rivers more space again?
a: Wide rivers can hold more water.
So that more ships can sail.
So that the river flows faster.
So that fewer fish live in it.
57612.e: A wide river bed takes in a lot of water, and the flood flows more slowly. It also creates valuable habitats.
57612.m: Rivers need space so that floods do less damage.

57613.q: Which valley in Ticino was hit by severe storms with flooding and debris flows in June 2024?
57613.e: At the end of June 2024, storms devastated mainly the upper Maggia Valley with the Val Bavona. Several people died.
57613.m: In June 2024 a severe storm hit the Maggia Valley.

57614.q: How are threatened mountain villages such as Bondo warned about rockfalls today?
57614.e: On Piz Cengalo, devices constantly measure whether the rock is moving. If there is danger, warnings go off and roads are closed.
57614.m: Measuring devices on the mountain warn of rockfalls.

57615.q: Roughly how fast did the masses of rock rush into the valley in the Bondo landslide?
57615.e: The masses of rock raced through the Val Bondasca at around 250 km/h. That is as fast as an express train.
57615.m: In the Bondo landslide, the rock raced into the valley at about 250 km/h.

57616.q: Which valley is the village of Bondo in?
57616.e: Bondo lies in the Bregaglia valley in the south of Graubünden, near the border with Italy.
57616.m: Bondo is in the Bregaglia valley in Graubünden.

57617.q: Roughly how much rock fell in the Bondo landslide in 2017?
57617.e: Around 3 million cubic metres of rock thundered from Piz Cengalo into the Val Bondasca. That is roughly 3000 family houses full of rock.
57617.m: About three million cubic metres of rock fell at Bondo.

57618.q: How many hikers died in the Bondo landslide?
57618.e: Eight hikers were in the Val Bondasca and were buried. They were never found.
57618.m: Eight people died in the Bondo landslide.

57619.q: What reached the village after the Bondo landslide and damaged houses?
57619.e: The fallen rock mixed with water and rubble to form debris flows. These flowed through the valley as far as Bondo.
57619.m: In Bondo, several debris flows followed the landslide.

57620.q: Which protective structure had been built in Bondo before 2017 and held back part of the material?
57620.e: After a rockfall in 2011, a catch basin with a protective wall was built. But in the big event of 2017 the basin was not enough for all the material.
57620.m: The catch basin in Bondo helped to limit the damage.

57621.q: Which language is spoken in the Bregaglia valley, where the village of Bondo is?
57621.e: The Bregaglia valley lies in the south of Graubünden on the border with Italy. Italian is spoken there.
57621.m: Italian is spoken in the Bregaglia valley.

57622.q: What does a protection forest in the mountains protect against?
57622.e: Trees hold snow, stones and soil in place. That way the protection forest protects villages, roads and railway lines.
57622.m: The protection forest stops avalanches and rockfall.

57623.q: Roughly what share of Swiss forest is protection forest?
57623.e: Around half of Switzerland's forest area protects people and property from natural hazards.
57623.m: About half of Swiss forest is protection forest.

57624.q: What is generally forbidden in Swiss forests under the Forest Act?
57624.e: In clear-cutting, a large area is cut down completely. This is forbidden because the soil would otherwise be unprotected and natural hazards would increase.
57624.m: Clear-cutting is forbidden in Swiss forests.

57625.q: Why are felled tree trunks in a protection forest often left lying across the slope?
a: They slow down sliding snow and stones.
They serve as benches for hikers.
They are dried there for firewood.
They keep deer away from the forest.
57625.e: Trunks lying across the slope and tall stumps act like small barriers. They hold back snow and stones until young trees have grown.
57625.m: Trunks lying across the slope protect against rockfall and avalanches.

57626.q: Why is too much browsing by wild animals a problem for the protection forest?
a: The old trees fall over at once.
57626.e: Red deer, roe deer and chamois eat the buds and shoots of young trees. Without young growth the forest gets too old and protects less well.
57626.m: Without young trees the protection forest loses its strength.

57627.q: Which kind of forest protects best against natural hazards?
a: A mixed forest with old and young trees
A forest with trees all the same age
A forest with no young trees at all
A cleared slope with tree stumps
57627.e: A layered forest with trees of every age stays stable, even when single trees die.

57628.q: Why did the federal government protect mountain forests with a law from 1876?
a: After clearing there were severe floods
Because there were too many trees
57628.e: Many slopes had been cleared, and rainwater flowed unchecked into the valley. After big floods, the federal government banned large-scale clearing in the mountains.
57628.m: A federal law has protected mountain forests since 1876.

57629.q: Which conifer grows in mountain forests up to the tree line and loses its needles in autumn?
57629.e: The larch is the only native conifer that sheds its needles in winter. It often grows in high protection forests.
57629.m: The larch loses its needles in autumn.

57630.q: In which year did a strong earthquake destroy the city of Basel?
57630.e: On 18 October 1356, the strongest known earthquake north of the Alps shook the city of Basel.
57630.m: Basel was destroyed by an earthquake in 1356.

57631.q: What caused further great damage in the city after the Basel earthquake of 1356?
57631.e: Hearth fires and lamps set the wooden houses alight. The fire is said to have raged for several days.
57631.m: After the earthquake, Basel burned for days.

57632.q: Which famous building in Basel was badly damaged in the earthquake of 1356?
57632.e: During the earthquake the choir of the Minster collapsed. The roof fell into the nave.
57632.m: Basel Minster was badly damaged in 1356.

57633.q: Roughly what magnitude do experts estimate for the Basel earthquake of 1356?
57633.e: Estimates range from around 6.0 to 7.0. It was the strongest known earthquake in Central Europe north of the Alps.
57633.m: The Basel earthquake had a magnitude of about 6 to 7.

57634.q: What was destroyed or damaged in large numbers in the area around Basel during the earthquake?
57634.e: Around 40 castles near Basel were damaged or destroyed. The damage reached as far as about 50 km away.
57634.m: Many castles around Basel collapsed in 1356.

57635.q: Why did probably fewer people die in the Basel earthquake of 1356 than you might expect?
a: Many fled after a first foreshock.
The city was uninhabited at the time.
The quake only happened under the Rhine.
57635.e: There was a first shock in the afternoon, and the strongest ones followed in the night. By then many people had already left the city.
57635.m: A foreshock warned many people in Basel in 1356.

57636.q: Which body in Switzerland records earthquakes and assesses the earthquake risk?
57636.e: The Swiss Seismological Service at ETH Zurich monitors earthquakes throughout the country.
57636.m: The Swiss Seismological Service monitors earthquakes.

57637.q: According to current knowledge, where was the epicentre of the Basel earthquake of 1356?
a: In the Black Forest near Freiburg
In the middle of the Jura near Biel
57637.e: Experts think the source was a few kilometres south of Basel, roughly under Reinach in Basel-Landschaft.
57637.m: The earthquake of 1356 had its source south of Basel.

57638.q: Which canton has the highest earthquake risk in Switzerland?
57638.e: Valais has the most earthquakes that people can feel. Next come the Basel region, Graubünden and Central Switzerland.
57638.m: Valais is the canton most at risk from earthquakes.

57639.q: Roughly how far does Switzerland stretch from west to east?
57639.e: From Chancy in the west to the Val Müstair in the east it is about 348 kilometres as the crow flies.
57639.m: From west to east, Switzerland measures about 350 kilometres.

57640.q: Roughly how far does Switzerland stretch from north to south?
57640.e: From Bargen in the canton of Schaffhausen to Chiasso in Ticino it is about 220 kilometres as the crow flies.
57640.m: From north to south, Switzerland measures about 220 kilometres.

57641.q: Which of the three main landscape regions covers the largest part of the country?
57641.e: The Alps cover around 60 percent of the area, the Central Plateau about 30 percent and the Jura about 10 percent.
57641.m: More than half of Switzerland lies in the Alps.

57642.q: Germany is about 357,000 km² in size. Roughly how many times does Switzerland fit into this area?
57642.e: 357,000 divided by 41,300 is about 8.6. So Switzerland fits into Germany about 9 times.
57642.m: Germany is almost nine times as big as Switzerland.

57643.q: Roughly what share of the population names German as their main language (as of 2023)?
57643.e: According to the Federal Statistical Office, around 61 percent named German as their main language in 2023, mostly in the form of Swiss German. More than one answer was possible.
57643.m: About three in five people in Switzerland have German as their main language.

57644.q: Which language is the second most common main language in Switzerland?
57644.e: After German, most people in Switzerland name French as their main language, especially in western Switzerland.
57644.m: French is the second most common main language in Switzerland.

57645.q: Roughly what share of the population names Italian as their main language (as of 2023)?
57645.e: According to the Federal Statistical Office, around 8 percent name Italian as their main language, mainly in Ticino and southern Graubünden.
57645.m: Italian is the main language of about 8 percent of the population.

57646.q: According to the Federal Constitution, which four languages are the national languages of Switzerland?
57646.e: The Federal Constitution names four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh. English is not a national language.

57647.q: In which languages does the federal government publish all of its laws in full?
57647.e: German, French and Italian are the full official languages of the Confederation. All laws appear in these three languages and are equally valid.
57647.m: Federal laws appear in German, French and Italian.

57648.q: What is Italian-speaking Switzerland, with Ticino and southern Graubünden, called in Italian?
57648.e: Svizzera italiana means “Italian Switzerland”. It includes the canton of Ticino and the Italian-speaking valleys of Graubünden.
57648.m: Italian-speaking Switzerland is called Svizzera italiana.

57649.q: In which municipality in Ticino has a German Walser dialect been spoken for over 600 years?
57649.e: Walser people from Valais founded Bosco/Gurin in the Middle Ages. Gurinerdeutsch is a language island in Italian-speaking Switzerland.
57649.m: A Walser dialect is spoken in Bosco/Gurin in Ticino.

57650.q: What is typical of many places on the German-French language border?
a: They have a German and a French name.
They are all on a lake.
They always belong to two cantons.
They have no name of their own.
57650.e: Examples are Biel and Bienne, Freiburg and Fribourg, or Siders and Sierre. The names show that both language groups know the place.
57650.m: Many places on the language border have two names.

57651.q: Near which town in Valais does the language border between German and French run?
57651.e: Sierre (Siders) is French-speaking, and a few kilometres further east people speak German.
57651.m: In Valais the language border runs near Sierre.

57652.q: Which pass links the German-speaking Goms with the Italian-speaking Bedretto Valley?
57652.e: The Nufenen Pass leads from Ulrichen in Valais to the Bedretto Valley in Ticino. At the top of the pass you cross the language border between German and Italian.
57652.m: At the Nufenen Pass the language changes from German to Italian.

57653.q: How many idioms, that is regional written languages, does Romansh have?
57653.e: The five idioms are Sursilvan, Sutsilvan, Surmiran, Puter and Vallader. Each valley has its own way of writing.

57654.q: What status has Romansh had at federal level since 1996?
57654.e: Since the vote of 10 March 1996, Romansh has been an official language of the Confederation when dealing with Romansh speakers.
57654.m: Romansh has been a partial official language of the Confederation since 1996.

57655.q: What is the common written language created for all Romansh speakers called?
57655.e: Rumantsch Grischun was created in 1982. The federal government and the canton of Graubünden use it for official texts.
57655.m: Rumantsch Grischun is the common written language of Romansh speakers.

57656.q: What does the Romansh greeting “Allegra” mean?
57656.e: People in Graubünden greet each other with “Allegra”. The word is related to “to be glad”.

57657.q: Which old language does Romansh come from?
57657.e: The Romans brought Latin to the Alps. In Graubünden it developed into Romansh.

57658.q: Which umbrella organisation has been working for the Romansh language since 1919?
57658.e: The Lia Rumantscha was founded in 1919 and unites the regional language associations.
57658.m: The Lia Rumantscha has promoted Romansh since 1919.

57659.q: Roughly how many people name Romansh as their main language (as of 2023)?
57659.e: Around 0.5 percent of the population, about 40,000 people, name Romansh as their main language. It is spoken mainly in Graubünden.
57659.m: Romansh is the smallest national language of Switzerland.

57660.q: Which neighbouring countries does the canton of Valais border?
57660.e: In the south, Valais borders Italy, for example at the Matterhorn. In the west, near Martigny and Monthey, it borders France.

57661.q: With which neighbouring country does Switzerland share the shortest border?
57661.e: The border with Liechtenstein is only about 41 kilometres long.
57661.m: Switzerland's shortest border is with Liechtenstein.

57662.q: Which neighbouring country has the most inhabitants?
57662.e: Germany has over 80 million inhabitants, France just under 70 million and Italy just under 60 million.
57662.m: Germany is Switzerland's most populous neighbour.

57663.q: Which neighbouring country borders both Graubünden and St Gallen?
57663.e: In the east, Austria borders the Rhine Valley in the canton of St Gallen and the Lower Engadine and Samnaun in Graubünden.
57663.m: Austria is the eastern neighbour of St Gallen and Graubünden.

57664.q: Which countries does the canton of Basel-Stadt border?
57664.e: Basel lies at the bend of the Rhine, where Switzerland, Germany and France meet.

57665.q: Roughly how long is Switzerland's national border?
57665.e: According to swisstopo, the national border is just under 2,000 kilometres long (around 1,970 km, as of 2018). A large part runs through the Alps and the Jura.
57665.m: Switzerland's border is almost 2,000 kilometres long.

57666.q: Which canton lies almost completely north of the Rhine?
57666.e: Most of the canton of Schaffhausen lies on the right bank of the Rhine. That is why it is surrounded by Germany on three sides.
57666.m: The canton of Schaffhausen lies almost entirely north of the Rhine.

57667.q: Which of these cantons has no border with another country?
57667.e: Lucerne lies in the middle of Switzerland. Aargau and Thurgau border Germany, and Jura borders France.
57667.m: The canton of Lucerne has no national border.

57668.q: Which authority checks at the Swiss border which goods are brought into the country?
57668.e: The Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS), formerly the Customs Administration, checks goods at the border and collects duties and taxes.
57668.m: Customs check the goods at the border.

57669.q: Which village in Graubünden is outside the customs area, so you can shop there duty-free?
57669.e: For a long time Samnaun could only be reached easily from Austria, so it is not part of the Swiss customs area.
57669.m: You can shop duty-free in Samnaun.

57670.q: Which lake is Campione d'Italia on?
57670.e: Campione d'Italia lies on the eastern shore of Lake Lugano, opposite Lugano.
57670.m: Campione d'Italia is on Lake Lugano.

57671.q: Which canton surrounds Campione d'Italia on the land side?
57671.e: On the land side, Campione only borders municipalities in Ticino. You reach Italy via Swiss roads.
57671.m: Campione d'Italia is surrounded by the canton of Ticino.

57672.q: What was Campione d'Italia especially known for for a long time?
57672.e: For a long time the Campione casino was one of the largest in Europe. It brought the small town a lot of money.
57672.m: Campione d'Italia is known for its casino.

57673.q: Which architect from Ticino designed the Campione d'Italia casino that opened in 2007?
57673.e: Mario Botta's new casino building opened in 2007. It was one of the largest casinos in Europe.
57673.m: The Campione casino was designed by the architect Mario Botta.

57674.q: Which number plates did vehicles from Campione d'Italia have until the end of 2019?
57674.e: Until the end of 2019, cars drove with Swiss number plates from the canton of Ticino. Since 2020 they have had to be registered in Italy.
57674.m: Cars from Campione used to have Ticino number plates.

57675.q: Which country code do most landlines in Campione d'Italia have?
57675.e: Almost all landlines are connected to the Swiss network. So anyone calling from Italy dials 0041.

57676.q: Who had the words “d'Italia” added to the place name Campione in 1933?
57676.e: The fascist dictator Mussolini added the words in 1933 to stress that the town belonged to Italy.
57676.m: Mussolini added “d'Italia” to the name in 1933.

57677.q: Which canton is the geographical centre of Switzerland in?
57677.e: The centre lies on the Älggi Alp above Sachseln in the canton of Obwalden.
57677.m: The centre of Switzerland is in the canton of Obwalden.

57678.q: Which method was used to work out the geographical centre of Switzerland?
a: As the centre of gravity of the country's area
As the midpoint between Basel and Chiasso
As the highest point in Central Switzerland
As the place with equal numbers of people all around
57678.e: The centre of gravity of the area was calculated. A cardboard cut-out of Switzerland could be balanced on a pin at this point.
57678.m: The centre is the centre of gravity of Switzerland's area.

57679.q: Where exactly is the geographical centre of Switzerland?
a: On an alpine pasture in the mountains
In the Federal Palace in Bern
In the old town of Lucerne
In the middle of Lake Lucerne
57679.e: The centre lies on the Älggi Alp above Sachseln. There is a memorial stone there that you can reach on foot.
57679.m: The centre of Switzerland is on an alpine pasture.

57680.q: Why is the memorial stone not exactly on the calculated centre?
a: The exact point is hard to reach.
The point is in a lake.
57680.e: The calculated point is above a rock face and is hard to reach. So the stone was put up about 500 metres away.
57680.m: The stone stands a little away from the exact centre.

57681.q: Which federal office draws the official national maps of Switzerland and also calculated its centre?
57681.e: The Federal Office of Topography, swisstopo for short, surveys Switzerland and makes the national maps. It also calculated the centre of the country.

57682.q: Which federal office publishes the national maps of Switzerland?
57682.e: Swisstopo surveys Switzerland and makes the official national maps at different scales.
57682.m: The national maps come from swisstopo.

57683.q: Which scale of national map is most often used for hiking?
57683.e: The 1:25,000 map shows lots of details such as paths, houses and contour lines. That is why it is very popular for hiking.
57683.m: The 1:25,000 national map is especially good for hiking.

57684.q: On a map with a scale of 1:25,000, a route measures 4 cm. How long is it in reality?
57684.e: 4 cm times 25,000 is 100,000 cm. That is 1,000 m, so 1 km.

57685.q: On a map with a scale of 1:50,000, a route measures 3 cm. How long is it in reality?
57685.e: 3 cm times 50,000 is 150,000 cm. That is 1,500 m, so 1.5 km.

57686.q: Two places are 12 km apart. How far apart are they on a 1:100,000 map?
57686.e: At 1:100,000, 1 cm equals one kilometre. So 12 km is 12 cm on the map.
57686.m: At 1:100,000, one centimetre stands for one kilometre.

57687.q: Which general is the first accurate map of the whole of Switzerland named after?
57687.e: General Dufour led the survey of Switzerland. The Dufour map was published from 1845. Switzerland's highest peak, the Dufourspitze, is also named after him.
57687.m: The first accurate map of Switzerland is called the Dufour map.

57688.q: What do contour lines on a national map show?
a: Lines that join points of the same height
57688.e: Each contour line joins points at the same height above sea level. When the lines are close together, the ground is steep.
57688.m: Contour lines close together show steep ground.

57689.q: Which place was the reference point of the old Swiss national coordinates LV03?
57689.e: The old Bern observatory was given the coordinates 600,000 and 200,000. The whole country was surveyed from there.
57689.m: The old national coordinates start from the Bern observatory.

57690.q: What coordinates did the reference point in Bern have in the old LV03 system?
57690.e: Bern was given large values on purpose so that all points in Switzerland would have positive coordinates.
57690.m: In the old system, Bern had the coordinates 600,000 and 200,000.

57691.q: Why is the east value always bigger than the north value in the Swiss coordinate system?
a: So that the two values cannot be mixed up
Because Switzerland is wider than it is long
Because counting starts in the east
Because Bern is in the east
57691.e: The zero point was moved so that all east values are above 480,000 and all north values are below 300,000. This rules out mix-ups.
57691.m: In the Swiss coordinate system you cannot mix up the east and north values.

57692.q: In the new LV95 system, which digit does every east value start with?
57692.e: In LV95, a 2 is put in front of the east value and a 1 in front of the north value, for example 2,600,000 / 1,200,000.
57692.m: In LV95 the east value starts with a 2.

57693.q: Which value is given first in Swiss national coordinates?
57693.e: First you give the east value (easting) and then the north value (northing).
57693.m: With national coordinates, the east value comes first.

57694.q: Point A has the coordinates 2,600,000 / 1,200,000, point B 2,603,000 / 1,204,000. How far apart are they as the crow flies?
57694.e: B lies 3,000 m east and 4,000 m north of A. By Pythagoras, the distance is the square root of 9 million plus 16 million, so 5,000 m.
57694.m: You use Pythagoras' theorem to work out distances between coordinates.

57695.q: A point has the east value 2,610,500 in LV95. How far east is it from a point with the east value 2,600,000?
57695.m: The difference between the east values gives the distance in metres.

57696.q: What are national coordinates used for?
a: To identify any place in Switzerland exactly
57696.e: With an east value and a north value you can find any point on the national map exactly.
57696.m: National coordinates pinpoint every place exactly.

57697.q: Which canton is the northernmost point of Switzerland in?
57697.e: The northernmost point is near Oberbargen in the municipality of Bargen in the canton of Schaffhausen.
57697.m: Switzerland's northernmost point is in the canton of Schaffhausen.

57698.q: Which canton is the southernmost point of Switzerland in?
57698.e: The southernmost point is near Pedrinate, part of Chiasso in the canton of Ticino.
57698.m: Switzerland's southernmost point is in Ticino.

57699.q: Which canton is the westernmost point of Switzerland in?
57699.e: The westernmost point is near Chancy in the canton of Geneva, where the Rhone leaves Switzerland.
57699.m: Switzerland's westernmost point is in the canton of Geneva.

57700.q: Which canton is the easternmost point of Switzerland in?
57700.e: The easternmost point is on Piz Chavalatsch in the Val Müstair in the canton of Graubünden, on the border with Italy.
57700.m: Switzerland's easternmost point is in Graubünden.

57701.q: Roughly how big is the height difference between the highest and the lowest point in Switzerland?
57701.m: There are about 4,400 metres of height between Switzerland's highest and lowest points.

57702.q: Which section of the Rhine forms the border with Germany between Lake Constance and Basel?
57702.e: The High Rhine flows from the Untersee at Stein am Rhein to Basel and forms the border with Germany for long stretches.
57702.m: The High Rhine separates most of Switzerland from Germany.

57703.q: What stands across the High Rhine in several places on the border with Germany?
57703.e: There are many run-of-river power stations on the High Rhine, for example at Rheinfelden or Eglisau. Because the border runs through the river, they often belong to both countries together.
57703.m: Border power stations on the High Rhine make electricity for both countries.

57704.q: Which large river forms part of the border with France at the far west of the canton of Geneva?
57704.e: Shortly before the Rhone leaves Switzerland, it forms the border with France. The French-Swiss power station Chancy-Pougny stands there.
57704.m: The Rhone forms part of the national border west of Geneva.

57705.q: With which country does the Tresa form the border at Ponte Tresa?
57705.e: Swiss Ponte Tresa in Ticino and Italian Lavena Ponte Tresa face each other across the Tresa. A border crossing runs over the bridge.
57705.m: At Ponte Tresa, the Tresa forms the border with Italy.

a: A river along which a border runs
A river that only flows in one country
57706.e: With a border river, one bank is in a different country or canton from the other. The border usually runs down the middle of the river.
57706.m: A border river separates two areas.

57707.q: Which town has the same name on both sides of the High Rhine, in Switzerland and in Germany?
57707.e: Laufenburg in Aargau and Laufenburg in Baden face each other across the Rhine and are joined by a bridge.
57707.m: There is a Laufenburg on both the Swiss and the German side of the Rhine.

57708.q: Why are the Rhine Falls not on the border, even though the Rhine forms the border in this region?
57708.e: At the Rhine Falls, Neuhausen (Schaffhausen) is on one bank and Laufen-Uhwiesen (Zurich) on the other. Both belong to Switzerland.
57708.m: The Rhine Falls lie entirely in Switzerland.

57709.q: How many cantons have more than one official language?
57709.e: Bern, Fribourg and Valais are bilingual, and Graubünden is trilingual.

57710.q: Which languages are official languages in the canton of Valais?
57710.e: In the west of the canton most people speak French, in the east German. Both languages are official languages.

57711.q: Which language do most people in the canton of Fribourg speak?
57711.e: Around two thirds of the people in the canton of Fribourg speak French, and about a quarter speak German.
57711.m: Most people in the canton of Fribourg speak French.

57712.q: What is the German-speaking part of the canton of Valais called?
57712.e: Upper Valais stretches from the Pfyn Forest to the Goms. Central Valais and Lower Valais are French-speaking.
57712.m: German is spoken in Upper Valais.

57713.q: In which multilingual canton is the village of Bivio, where German, Italian and Romansh are spoken side by side?
57713.e: Bivio lies on the Julier Pass in the canton of Graubünden. Because it is on old trade routes, several languages are common there.
57713.m: You can hear three languages in the Graubünden village of Bivio.

57714.q: Which valley in Graubünden is Italian-speaking?
57714.e: Italian-speaking Graubünden includes the Val Poschiavo, the Bregaglia, the Mesolcina and the Val Calanca.
57714.m: The Val Poschiavo is part of Italian-speaking Graubünden.

57715.q: Roughly what share of Switzerland's area is unproductive land such as rock, scree, glaciers and water?
57715.e: According to the 2018 land use statistics, around a quarter of Switzerland is unproductive, mainly in the high Alps. There are hardly any plants there that can be used.
57715.m: About a quarter of Switzerland is rock, ice and water.

57716.q: Roughly what share of Switzerland's area is used for farming, including alpine pastures?
57716.e: According to the 2018 land use statistics, around 36 percent of Switzerland is farmland, including the alpine pastures.
57716.m: Just over a third of Switzerland is used for farming.

57717.q: Roughly what share of Switzerland's area is settlement area with houses, roads and railway lines?
57717.e: According to the 2018 land use statistics, settlement areas make up just under 8 percent of Switzerland. They are growing mainly in the Central Plateau.
57717.m: Only a small part of Switzerland is built on.

57718.q: Which language that is not a national language is most often named as a main language in Switzerland?
57718.e: Around 6 percent of the population name English as one of their main languages (as of 2023). Next come Portuguese and Albanian with around 3 percent each.
57718.m: English is the most common main language that is not a national language.

57719.q: Who decides in Switzerland which official language a canton has?
57719.e: Under the Federal Constitution, the cantons decide their official languages. In doing so, they respect the traditional language of their area.
57719.m: Each canton decides its own official languages.

57720.q: Which canton is NOT crossed by the German-French language border?
57720.e: Vaud is completely French-speaking. Bern, Fribourg and Valais have German-speaking and French-speaking areas.
57720.m: Vaud lies entirely in the Romandie.

57721.q: Which pine forest in Valais is seen as the natural language border between German and French?
57721.e: The Pfyn Forest (Bois de Finges in French) near Leuk is one of the largest pine forests in the Alps. East of it people speak German, west of it French.
57721.m: The Pfyn Forest separates German and French in Valais.

57722.q: Which holiday resort lies in the German-speaking Saanenland, just a few kilometres from the language border?
57722.e: Gstaad belongs to the Bernese municipality of Saanen. In nearby Rougemont in the canton of Vaud, people already speak French.
57722.m: Gstaad lies close to the language border.

57723.q: In which canton is Romansh mainly spoken?
57723.e: Romansh is spoken mainly in valleys of Graubünden, for example in the Surselva and the Engadine.

57724.q: What is the SRG's radio and television service in Romansh called?
57724.e: RTR stands for Radiotelevisiun Svizra Rumantscha and is based in Chur. RSI broadcasts in Italian, RTS in French.
57724.m: RTR is the SRG's Romansh broadcaster.

57725.q: Which neighbouring country, like Switzerland, is not a member of the European Union?
57725.e: Liechtenstein is not in the EU, but it is a member of the European Economic Area (EEA). All the other neighbouring countries are EU members.
57725.m: Like Switzerland, Liechtenstein is not in the EU.

57726.q: Which agreement does Switzerland belong to, which is why there have been no systematic passport checks at the borders since 2008?
57726.e: Switzerland has applied the Schengen Agreement since December 2008. Customs checks on goods still take place, though.
57726.m: Thanks to Schengen, there are no systematic passport checks at the border.

a: An area of a country that is completely surrounded by foreign territory
A border crossing in the mountains
An island in the middle of a river
57727.e: An exclave is separated from the main territory of its country. From the point of view of the surrounding country, it is called an enclave.
57727.m: An exclave is cut off from its own country.

57728.q: Which currency is official in Campione d'Italia today?
57728.e: The euro is official because Campione belongs to Italy. In the past people mostly paid with Swiss francs in everyday life.
57728.m: The euro is official in Campione d'Italia.

57729.q: Which Swiss national saint is buried in Sachseln, the municipality that the geographical centre belongs to?
57729.e: Nicholas of Flüe, known as Brother Klaus, is buried in the parish church of Sachseln. He lived in the Ranft in the 15th century.
57729.m: Brother Klaus is buried in Sachseln.

57730.q: In which main landscape region is the geographical centre of Switzerland?
57730.e: The centre lies in the Central Swiss Alps. This shows that the Alps take up a large part of Switzerland.
57730.m: The centre of Switzerland is in the Alps.

57731.q: Which Swiss cartographer became world-famous for his artistic relief shading on maps?
57731.e: Eduard Imhof (1895 to 1986) was a professor at ETH Zurich. His way of showing landscape with shading and colour shapes Swiss cartography.
57731.m: Eduard Imhof made Swiss relief maps famous.

57732.q: In which bilingual canton do most people speak German?
57732.e: In the canton of Bern, the great majority speak German. In Fribourg and Valais, French is the majority language.
57732.m: In the bilingual canton of Bern, most people speak German.

57733.q: What is Sitten, the capital of the canton of Valais, called in French?
57733.e: Sitten lies in French-speaking Lower Valais. In French the town is called Sion.
57733.m: The Valais capital Sitten is called Sion in French.

57734.q: Which language do most people speak in the trilingual canton of Graubünden?
57734.e: Around three quarters of the people of Graubünden mainly speak German. Romansh and Italian are minority languages in the canton.
57734.m: Most people in Graubünden speak German.

57735.q: What material was the Colossus of Rhodes made of?
57735.e: The Colossus was built from bronze plates over a frame of iron and stone. It is said to have been over 30 metres tall.
57735.m: The Colossus of Rhodes was a huge bronze statue.

57736.q: In which ancient city are the Hanging Gardens said to have been?
57736.e: The Hanging Gardens of Semiramis are said to have been in Babylon, in what is now Iraq. To this day it is disputed whether they really existed.
57736.m: The Hanging Gardens are linked with Babylon.

57737.q: Which god did the Colossus of Rhodes represent?
57737.e: The people of Rhodes dedicated the statue to their protector god Helios. It stood at the harbour of the city of Rhodes.
57737.m: The Colossus of Rhodes showed the sun god Helios.

57738.q: Which ancient wonder of the world stood in the harbour of Alexandria in Egypt?
57738.e: The lighthouse stood on the island of Pharos off Alexandria and showed ships the way. The French word ‘phare’ for lighthouse comes from the name Pharos.
57738.m: A famous lighthouse stood in Alexandria.

57739.q: Which Greek god did the huge seated statue of gold and ivory in Olympia show?
57739.e: The statue showed Zeus, father of the gods, on his throne. It was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
57739.m: The famous statue of Zeus stood in Olympia.

57740.q: In which present-day country was the Temple of Artemis at Ephesus?
57740.e: Ephesus lay on the west coast of Asia Minor, which today belongs to Turkey. The huge temple was dedicated to the goddess Artemis.
57740.m: The Temple of Artemis at Ephesus stood in present-day Turkey.

57741.q: Which word comes from the tomb of King Mausolus at Halicarnassus?
57741.e: The magnificent tomb for King Mausolus was considered a wonder of the world. Since then, large tombs have been called ‘mausoleums’.
57741.m: Large tombs are called mausoleums after King Mausolus.

57743.q: Which culture do the lists of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World come from?
57743.e: Greek writers such as Antipater of Sidon put together the lists of wonders. That is why all the buildings are around the Mediterranean and in the Middle East.
57743.m: The list of ancient wonders comes from Greek writers.

57744.q: In which year were the New Seven Wonders of the World announced?
57744.e: Millions of people had voted online and by phone. The seven winners were announced in July 2007.
57744.m: The New Seven Wonders of the World were chosen in 2007.

57745.q: Whose idea was the vote for the New Seven Wonders of the World?
